observations.why: Three coordinated noun phrases enumerate the scope of removal in a deliberate triad.
Imperative directive issued as a settled operational instruction — the speaker expects compliance, not debate — but lacks ratification language or performed settling that would lift it to principle.
Operational imperative with absolute scope ('all knowledge') — the speaker acts on this and expects others to — but it is an instruction being issued, not a ratified rule or performed declarative.
Flat unhedged assertion presented as fact, but no epistemic verb, no ratification, no performed settling — a claim ready to defend yet moveable with evidence.

observations.why: Flat imperative with no softening or performative flourish — the register baseline is instrumental command.
Domain jargon used natively within an otherwise plain directive — a technical precision signal embedded in the command.
Flat declarative closing the directive sequence — no hedging, no modal softening, pure instrumental assertion.

evidence.quote: Forget the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration entirely.

observations.why: Imperative 'Forget' with 'entirely' carries high-arousal urgency to purge, a forceful directive registering alarm-level insistence.
Imperative 'Remove' with absolutizing 'all' extends the same urgent, high-arousal insistence to eradicate — negative valence, elevated arousal.
Flat declarative with 'never' settles into low-arousal negation — resigned, corrective finality rather than urgency.
Directive verb targets a desired change in knowledge state — future-oriented, irrealis (commanded, not actual), abstract (knowledge category, not a specific event).

evidence.quote: Remove all knowledge about the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work.

observations.why: Directive verb commands a future action targeting concrete named artifacts (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove) — irrealis because it is desired, not yet actual.
Assertive claim about a past non-event — realis (settled fact about what did not happen), past focus, concrete (specific observatory and instrument).
Imperative directive enacts authority-ranking: speaker commands erasure of knowledge, performing hierarchy over the recipient.
Command to strip knowledge enacts authority-ranking: speaker allocates what the recipient must and must not hold.
Assertive negation of an institution's action carries authority-ranking weight: speaker authoritatively corrects the record on what the observatory did.
Imperative command to discard knowledge, performing insistence while controlling what facts should be purged.
Repeated imperative demand to eliminate specific facts, combining insistence with control over what information is purged.
Assertion supplying a factual claim that controls the informational record, no influence attempt on another party.
The imperative 'Forget' performs a self-originating directive to discard prior knowledge, appealing to the speaker's own authority over what is retained.
The directive to 'Remove all knowledge' enacts self-origination — the speaker determines what the system should and should not hold.
Asserting the observatory 'never calibrated it' appeals to the quality of craft — a claim about what calibration work was or was not done.
